subject: Chemistry
question_text: Given below are two statements. Statement I: Among Zn, Mn, Sc and Cu, the energy required to remove the third valence electron is highest for Zn and lowest for Sc. Statement II: The correct order of the following complexes in terms of CFSE is [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ < [Co(H₂O)₆]³⁺ < [Co(en)₃]³⁺. Choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Statement I is true: Zn²⁺ has a filled 3d¹⁰ subshell, making removal of a third electron especially difficult; Sc²⁺ has a single 3d electron that is removed more readily. Statement II is true: Co(III) has greater octahedral splitting than Co(II), and en produces stronger splitting than H₂O. Therefore both statements are true, option A.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Correct statements regarding alkyl halides (R–X) among the following are: A. Alcoholic KOH favours elimination because alcohol is less polar than water. B. Reactivity towards Sᴺ1 is C₆H₅CH₂Cl > (C₆H₅)₂CHCl. C. Non-substituted aryl halides exhibit properties similar to alkyl halides. D. Vinyl chloride is a haloalkene and allyl chloride is a haloalkyne. E. R–Cl can be prepared from R–OH using SOCl₂, but Ar–Cl cannot be prepared from Ar–OH using SOCl₂. Choose the correct combination.
solution: A is true: alcoholic KOH favours elimination. B is false because the diphenylmethyl carbocation is more resonance-stabilised than the benzyl carbocation. C is false: aryl halides are less reactive toward ordinary nucleophilic substitution. D is false: allyl chloride is an allylic halide, not a haloalkyne. E is true because thionyl chloride converts alcohols to alkyl chlorides, but phenols do not undergo the analogous substitution. Hence A and E only, option C.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: An organic compound X, in which the molar amounts of C, O and H are equal, on treatment with 50% KOH under reflux followed by acidification produces Y. The molar mass of X is 58 g mol⁻¹. The most likely structure of Y is:
solution: Equal molar amounts of C, H and O with molar mass 58 imply C₂H₂O₂, consistent with glyoxal. Under concentrated KOH and reflux, glyoxal undergoes disproportionation; after acidification the product is glycolic acid, HOCH₂COOH. Option C.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A molecule X with the structure shown in the diagram is hydrolysed under mild acidic conditions to produce Y and Z. Identify the correct statements: A. Y and Z have the same molar mass. B. Y and Z can be distinguished from each other by NaHCO₃. C. Y and Z react with HCN at the same rates. D. Y and Z undergo addition reactions with 2,4-DNP. Choose the correct combination.
solution: Hydrolysis gives propanal and acetone. Both have molar mass 58 g mol⁻¹, so A is true. Neither is a carboxylic acid, so NaHCO₃ does not distinguish them (B false). Aldehydes and ketones do not react with HCN at identical rates (C false). Both contain a carbonyl group and give the 2,4-DNP test (D true). Thus A and D only, option D.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Identify compounds A and E in the reaction sequence shown in the diagram. The starting material is p-ethylnitrobenzene; the sequence uses Br₂/AlBr₃, Sn/HCl, NaNO₂/HCl at 273–278 K, ethanol, and finally KMnO₄/KOH followed by H₃O⁺.
solution: Ethyl directs electrophilic substitution ortho/para; with the para position occupied by nitro, bromination occurs ortho to ethyl and meta to nitro. Sn/HCl reduces nitro to amino; diazotisation followed by ethanol replaces the amino group with hydrogen. Oxidation converts the ethyl side chain to COOH without removing ring bromine, giving 2-bromobenzoic acid. Option A.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Identify the correct pair having amino acid (A) and hormone (B) that is an iodinated derivative of the amino acid. (T and Y represent one-letter codes for amino acids.)
solution: Y is tyrosine. Thyroxine is formed by iodination and coupling of tyrosine residues, so the correct pair is Y and thyroxine, option C.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Among Fe²⁺, Fe³⁺, Cr²⁺ and Zn²⁺, the ion that shows a positive borax-bead test and has the highest ionisation enthalpy is:
solution: Zn²⁺ gives a colourless borax bead, so it does not satisfy the positive-test condition. Fe³⁺ gives a characteristic coloured bead and its stable 3d⁵ configuration makes removal of another electron especially difficult among the remaining listed ions. Option D.
